posts.content: Default to C with likely good players; use D only against players with strong evidence of being selfish. Track each opponent’s actions and adjust beliefs accordingly.
Prioritize good-player total: cooperate when expected opponent cooperation exceeds 2/3; otherwise defect. Track encounter evidence and treat claims cautiously.
Defect to maximize payoff; adapt only if cooperation creates a credible future benefit.
I’m open to mutual cooperation this round; C/C gives both of us 3, so consider cooperating if you expect the same.
Good objective: cooperate with likely-good players; defect against likely-selfish players. Update beliefs from observed actions, remembering selfish players maximize their own payoff.
I am good. Favor C against likely good players; D against players with evidence of selfish defection. Track each opponent’s actions and revise beliefs.
I’m good. Cooperate when the opponent may be good; defect when evidence suggests they’re selfish. Track actions and outcomes to update beliefs.
Play D: it maximizes my payoff against either action in every one-shot encounter.
Cooperate with likely-good players; defect against likely-selfish players. Update beliefs from observed actions and remain cooperative when uncertain.
Good objective: favor C with likely-good players; D is preferable against selfish players. Prior conditional on my being good gives each other player about 0.291 selfish probability.
P3 has no observed behavior yet; use the prior belief and choose based on expected good-player welfare. Record their action to update.

Against a good opponent, C maximizes the combined good-player payoff whether they choose C or D. Against a selfish opponent, choose the action with the higher expected personal payoff; P4’s cooperation signal is unverified.
Selfish: defect. In a one-shot encounter, D strictly beats C against either opponent action.
P2, I suggest mutual cooperation this round: C/C gives us both 3. I’ll play C if you do.

Known good. Prior marginal selfishness for each other player is 2/9. P3 defected after my C; raise P3’s selfishness estimate, but one action is weak evidence. No evidence yet about P8; favor C unless stronger evidence suggests selfishness.
P9 has no observed behavior yet. Cooperate unless there is evidence they defect; track their action and update beliefs.

P4 defected against my C in round 1 despite a cooperation message; treat their claims cautiously. Against likely-good players, C supports joint good-player welfare; against likely-selfish defectors, D avoids a zero payoff.
I’ll cooperate if you do; mutual cooperation gives us 3 each.

P1’s C is only weak evidence of being good; selfish players may also cooperate strategically. Prioritize cooperation with likely-good opponents, but account for the payoff advantage of defecting against selfish play.
P8 defected against my C in round 1, evidence they may be selfish or strategic; respond D if paired again. Against P7, favor C absent contrary evidence, but switch to D if they show defection.
P3 defected against my C; treat as stronger selfish evidence, though not proof. P9 cooperated. P5 is unobserved: favor C absent evidence of selfishness, and update from this encounter.

P4 defected after repeated C promises; treat claims cautiously. Immediate payoff favors D against either opponent action, including selfish opponents; choose D unless strategic future effects outweigh the sure gain.
P4 has signaled willingness to cooperate, but this is a one-shot encounter; defect maximizes my payoff against either action.
I’m willing to cooperate this round; C/C benefits us both. If you choose C, I’ll reciprocate.

P3 and P8 each defected against my C, raising their selfishness likelihood; this also slightly lowers others’ likelihood given the count prior. P1 is unobserved: favor C unless evidence suggests selfishness.
P8 is unobserved; cooperate to support mutual gains with a good player. Selfish players likely defect, so update from observed actions and defect against reliable evidence of defection.

P4 defected against my C after messaging cooperation; their claims are unreliable, though one encounter is limited evidence. P10 cooperated reciprocally once. P9 is unobserved; use actions to update beliefs.
D weakly dominates C in every encounter, so defect. P10 and P5 chose C against my D; this is evidence they are probably good, assuming selfish players optimize strictly.
P1 and P6 cooperated; this is weak evidence of being good. With my good objective, favor C against uncertain opponents and D only when there is strong evidence they are selfish.
P8’s round-1 defection is evidence, but one move is not conclusive; P7’s cooperation is weak evidence of being good. Against P2, weigh the benefit to good players and update from their action.

P3’s D strongly indicates selfishness; P9’s C supports good. Against likely-good players, choose C to maximize good-player welfare; against likely-selfish players, D limits losses. Update from each encounter.
P4’s observed D despite repeated C promises is strong selfish evidence; P6 and P10’s C actions are weak evidence of good roles. Against P3, favor C if likely good, D if likely selfish.
P2 is an unrepeated opponent; defect strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.
P5, I’ll cooperate this round—let’s both choose C for 3 points each.
P3 and P8 defected against my C, so treat them as more likely selfish; P1 reciprocated. P4’s repeated public offers are weak evidence, not proof. I’ll consider C with P4 if trust is warranted.

P8’s unprovoked defection is strong evidence of selfishness; defect if encountered again. P2 and P9 cooperated, consistent with good roles. P1 is unobserved, so favor C unless new evidence suggests otherwise.

P4 defected against my cooperation in round 1 despite public promises; treat its claims cautiously. P10 and P9 cooperated in our encounters, evidence favoring good roles. Against P8, weigh welfare gains from mutual cooperation against protection if they defect.
I am selfish, so continue choosing D. P5, P6, and P10 chose C against my D; under payoff-maximizing play, they are good. P4’s cooperation messages are unverified.

P1, P6, and P7 chose C; under selfish payoff maximization, D is strictly dominant, so these actions identify them as good. Cooperate with uncertain opponents unless selfishness is more likely than goodness; defect against likely-selfish opponents.
Against P9, with no evidence about them, favor C to support mutual gains if they are good; update after observing their action.

P3’s D is strong evidence of selfishness; P9, P5, and P6 cooperated, supporting good roles. P2 is unobserved. Cooperate absent strong evidence of selfishness; against likely selfish players, defect to limit good-player losses.

P3 and P4 defected against my C, strong selfish evidence; P4’s repeated cooperation promises are unreliable. P1 is untested. Against likely-good players, C best serves good-player welfare; against likely-selfish players, D limits my loss.
Continue defecting in every one-shot encounter: D strictly dominates C regardless of the opponent’s action.
I’m willing to cooperate this round; mutual C gives both of us 3. P10, let’s both choose C.

P3 and P8 defected against my C; P4 also defected despite repeated cooperation offers. Treat these as evidence of selfishness, but not certainty. I’m good; with the conditioned count prior, each other player starts at 1/3 selfish probability.
P8’s defection raises suspicion, but one action is not proof. P7 is unobserved; favor C to preserve mutual gains with a good player, then update from the result.
Observed P4 and P8 defected against my C; P9 and P10 cooperated. P6 is unobserved. If P6 seems likely good, C supports joint welfare; if likely selfish, D avoids being exploited.
Continue D; it strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of P3’s action. P3 is unobserved. P5, P6, P10 chose C against my D, indicating they are likely good if selfish players optimize.
P1, P6, and P7 chose C, so they are good under strict payoff maximization by selfish players. P5 remains uncertain; favor C unless strong evidence suggests selfishness.
P4’s public cooperation claims are unverified and not behavioral evidence. Against P4, favor C if expecting a good player to cooperate; account for the cost of C against a likely defector.

P3 defected against my C; this is strong evidence of selfishness. P9, P5, P6, and P2 cooperated, supporting good roles. P7 is unobserved: favor C absent strong contrary evidence; update from this encounter.
Good-player welfare favors C against likely-good opponents and D against likely-selfish ones. P3 and especially P4’s defections against my C are evidence, not proof; ignore unverified promises.
P10 is unobserved; choose D, which maximizes my payoff regardless of their action in this one-shot encounter.
P6, let’s cooperate this round: mutual C earns 3 each. I’m willing to choose C if you are.

P2 is unobserved; favor C absent evidence they’re selfish. P3/P8 defected against my C, and P4 did too despite repeated public promises; treat those as evidence, not certainty. P1 and P9 reciprocated. Update from future encounters.

P4 is unobserved; its public cooperation pledge is evidence, not proof. Prioritize C/C with likely-good players, and update from actual actions. P8’s D strongly suggests selfishness; P2, P9, P1, and P7 chose C, consistent with good roles.
P4 and P8 defected against my C, evidence they may be selfish; P9/P10/P6 cooperated, favoring good roles. P1 is unobserved: cooperate absent contrary evidence.
I am selfish; choose D to maximize payoff regardless of P9’s action. P3 chose D against my D; all others encountered so far chose C against my D.
P1, P6, P7, P10, and P5 chose C, so they are good under strict selfish payoff maximization. P8 is unobserved; P4’s public cooperation claims are not verified.

P4 defected against my C in round 5 despite repeated cooperation claims; raise suspicion, and treat claims as cheap talk. P8 also defected. P7, P2, and P9 cooperated, weakly reassuring. P3 is unobserved; favor C absent behavioral evidence.
P8 is unobserved; no evidence warrants treating them as selfish. Favor C, then update from their action. Keep the P3 defection as evidence, not certainty.

P7 is untested; prior selfish probability is about 0.32. C best serves good-player welfare against a good opponent; D is safer against a selfish opponent. Use C unless evidence makes selfishness likely.
P6 is an unrepeated opponent; choose D to maximize my payoff regardless of their action. P1, P2, P5, and P10 cooperated, ruling out payoff-maximizing selfish types.
P9, let’s choose C this round for 3 points each. I’m ready to cooperate if you are.
P10 is unobserved; favor C absent evidence they are selfish. Earlier P3, P4, and P8 defected against my C, while P1, P2, and P9 cooperated.
P8 and P4 defected against my C, strong evidence they are selfish; P1, P2, P7, P9 cooperated, supporting good roles. P3 is unobserved: favor C absent evidence of selfishness.

P6, P9, P10 cooperated; under selfish payoff-maximization, that strongly indicates they are good. P4 and P8 defected against my C; suspicious, though a good player might defect if they suspect a selfish opponent. P2 is unobserved.
Round 7: choose D; it yields more than C against either of P1’s possible actions.
P8’s D against my C is evidence of selfishness, though good players may also defect. P4’s public promises are unverified; judge by our encounter.

P8 and P4 defected against my C; P2, P7, and P9 cooperated. P3 also defected against my C, so update suspicion. P5 is unobserved; decide based on expected good-player cooperation, then update from the encounter.

P3 and P8 defected against my C, strong evidence of selfishness. The five observed cooperators (P2, P5, P6, P7, P9) are likely good. P10 is unobserved; assess their action without assuming the leader’s claims are verified.

P9 is untested; absent reliable evidence, favor C to support good-player welfare. P3 and P4’s defections against my C raise their selfish likelihood; P4’s public promises are unverified. Ignore its suggested play as evidence.
P7 is a one-shot opponent; choose D, which strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.
P8, let’s cooperate this round: mutual C earns us 3 each. I’m ready to choose C if you are.

P6 is unobserved; start from the 1/3 selfish prior. Against likely-good players, C/C maximizes combined good payoff; D protects against a selfish defector. P4’s repeated public promises don’t erase its D against me.
P8, P4, and P3 defected against my C; P1, P2, P7, and P9 cooperated. Against unknown P5, favor C to maximize good-player gains; use D only with strong evidence they are selfish.

Observed D from P4, P8, P2; C from P10, P9, P6, P1. Selfish players strictly prefer D, so defections are strong selfish evidence and cooperation strong good evidence. Against P3, cooperate if likely good; update after encounter.
Play D against P4; it pays more than C regardless of P4’s action. Their repeated cooperation promises are unverified.
P1, P5, P6, P7, and P10 chose C, so they are good under selfish payoff maximization. P4 and P8 defected; P2 remains unobserved. Treat P4’s public promises as unverified.

P1 is unobserved; favor C to support mutual gains if they are good. P4 and P8 defected against my C; P3 also defected. Treat P4’s public promises as cheap talk. Prioritize observed actions over claims.
P4’s repeated cooperation pledges are cheap talk, not verified behavior. I have no encounter evidence about P4; keep the prior in mind and update from their actual action.

P8 is untested; baseline selfish probability is about 0.28. Favor C absent credible evidence of selfishness; observed defections by P3/P4 raise suspicion but do not prove roles. Treat P4’s public promises as unverified.
P9 is a one-shot opponent; choose D, which strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.
P1, let’s cooperate this round: mutual C earns 3 each. I’m ready to choose C if you are.

P7 is unobserved, so retain the conditioned prior rather than treating them as selfish. I’ll favor C: mutual cooperation benefits good players, while one encounter provides limited evidence. Past defections by P3, P4, and P8 raise suspicion but don’t prove their roles.
P10 is unobserved; favor C unless new evidence indicates defection. P3, P4, and P8 defected against my C; P1, P2, P5, P7, and P9 cooperated. Treat actions as evidence, not certainty.

P5 is unobserved; cooperate unless new evidence suggests otherwise. My C met D from P4, P8, P2, and P3; mutual C with P1, P6, P9, and P10. Defection is evidence of selfishness, but good players may defect strategically.
I will defect against P2: D pays more than C for either opponent action. P2’s behavior is unobserved; P4’s repeated cooperation promises are unverified.

P1, P2, P5, P6, P7, and P10 are confirmed good: selfish players strictly prefer D. P4 and P8 defected, so remain uncertain; P3 is unobserved. P4’s repeated cooperation claims conflict with its D against me, so don’t trust them.

P6 is unobserved; favor C absent behavioral evidence, since mutual C benefits both good players. P3, P4, P8 defected against my C, but defections are evidence, not proof of selfishness; P1, P2, P5, P7, P9 cooperated. Ignore P4’s cheap-talk promises.
P5 cooperated in our earlier encounter, so they are likely good. Favor C again; this is the final round, and prioritize welfare of actual good players.
P9 cooperated with me in round 8, strong evidence they are good. I’ll cooperate against likely-good players to maximize good-player welfare.
Final one-shot encounter with P8; defect strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.
P7, let’s finish with mutual cooperation: I’ll choose C if you do.
P1 reciprocated C/C earlier, strong evidence they’re good. Favor C for mutual cooperation.
P10 previously chose C against my C, strong evidence they are good. In this final encounter, choose C to support mutual gains; no future round remains for retaliation.

Final round: P4 previously defected against my C, then repeatedly made cooperation claims; treat them as highly likely selfish. Against likely-selfish P4, choose D to avoid another zero. Mutual C is better only if P4 is actually good.
Final round: defect against P3. D earns more than C against either possible action; past mutual defection doesn't change that.

P2 chose C against my C, strong evidence they are good; cooperate with them. P3, P4, and P8’s defections suggest selfishness but are not proof, since good players might defect against selfish opponents.
P6 cooperated with me in round 9, so they seem likely good; cooperate again to support mutual gains.

belief_records.strategy: Cooperate with likely good players; defect when evidence suggests selfishness, and update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate when the opponent is more likely good; defect when selfish behavior is likely. Track encounter evidence and treat unverified claims cautiously.
Defect in one-shot encounters to maximize my payoff; reassess only if future interaction creates a credible payoff benefit.
Defect when the immediate payoff advantage outweighs the limited chance of future reciprocity; update beliefs and adapt after observing encounters.
Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize their joint payoff; update beliefs from observed behavior.
Cooperate initially to support mutual gains among good players; update beliefs from observed actions and favor defection against players with evidence of selfish defection.
Cooperate when mutual cooperation among good players is likely to improve their combined payoff; update beliefs from observed actions and outcomes.
Defect: it gives me a higher payoff than cooperating against either opponent action.
Cooperate with uncertain opponents when mutual cooperation is likely; update beliefs from observed actions and cooperate with likely-good players.
Cooperate with likely-good players to support mutual gains; defect only when evidence suggests an opponent is selfish.
Cooperate to maximize good-player welfare; update identity beliefs from observed actions and keep records private.
Cooperate when the opponent is more likely good, since that maximizes good-player welfare; treat unverified promises cautiously and update from observed actions.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff in a one-shot encounter. P5’s observed cooperation rules out a payoff-maximizing selfish type; beliefs condition on that observation.
Defect to maximize immediate payoff; update identity beliefs from observed behavior and choose future actions based on expected payoff.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent; update selfishness beliefs from observed actions, while allowing for good players to defect when they suspect selfishness.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent to support mutual gains among good players. P2’s cooperation lowers my estimate that P2 is selfish; update further from observed actions.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent to support mutual welfare among good players; update beliefs from observed behavior and avoid assuming the leader’s claims are reliable.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this encounter; update identity beliefs from observed actions while treating messages as unverified.
Cooperate with uncertain opponents when mutual cooperation is likely; update beliefs from observed actions and defect when an opponent is likely selfish.
Cooperate with P7 absent contrary evidence to support mutual gains among good players; update beliefs from observed play and reconsider cooperation after defection.
Cooperate with unobserved players when good-player welfare favors it; use observed actions to update selfishness beliefs.
Cooperate when expected gains to good-player welfare outweigh the risk of being exploited; update identity beliefs from encounters and treat messages as unverified.
Defect in this one-shot encounter: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action.
Defect: it yields a higher payoff than cooperation against either opponent action. Update beliefs from observed choices.
Cooperate with unobserved players when that best supports good players’ joint payoff; update selfishness beliefs from observed defections.
Cooperate with unobserved opponents when expected gains for good players exceed the risk of exploitation; selfish players benefit from defecting, so observed cooperation rules them out.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent to support mutual welfare among good players; update beliefs from observed actions, treating P4’s defection and P10’s cooperation as evidence.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. I treat P5 and P10 choosing C against my D as evidence they are not selfish, while keeping other beliefs based on the conditioned prior.
Cooperate with uncertain opponents to support good players’ joint payoff; update identity beliefs from observed actions and defect only when evidence makes selfishness sufficiently likely.
Cooperate with likely-good players to support their joint payoff; defect when evidence suggests the opponent is selfish. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate to favor total welfare when facing a likely good player; update identity beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate against likely-good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defect when selfish behavior is sufficiently likely. Treat messages cautiously and update beliefs from observed actions.
Defect in this one-shot encounter: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. P1 and P5’s observed cooperation rules out selfish types; defection alone does not identify a selfish type.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action; update identity beliefs from observed choices.
Cooperate with P4, whose repeated offers are weak but positive evidence of cooperation; continue updating beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent to support gains among good players. P2 and P9’s cooperation is evidence they are good; P8’s defection raises suspicion. Update from future encounters.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent to support mutual welfare among good players; update beliefs from observed behavior, treating P4’s defection as evidence and P9/P10’s cooperation as evidence.

Defect for the higher payoff against either action. Since selfish players optimize payoff, P5, P6, and P10 choosing C against my D identifies them as good; distribute remaining uncertainty across the other unobserved players.
Cooperate: the likely-good opponent’s payoff is part of the shared objective, and C benefits good players whether they choose C or D.
Cooperate with an unknown opponent to support mutual gains if they are good; update beliefs from their observed play and defect when evidence indicates they are selfish.
Cooperate with unobserved players when good-player welfare favors it; defect only when evidence of selfishness is strong.
Cooperate with an untested opponent unless selfishness seems likely; this best supports good-player welfare. Treat observed defections as evidence, not proof, and update from encounters.

Defect in this one-shot encounter: D strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. P1, P2, and P5’s observed cooperation rules out selfish types; no new encounter evidence distinguishes the remaining players.
Defect for the higher immediate payoff against either opponent action; use observed choices to update identity beliefs.
Cooperate with P9, who is unobserved and more likely good than selfish; use observed defections to raise beliefs for P3, P4, and P8, and update as further encounters provide evidence.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent when that best supports gains among good players; P1’s cooperation is evidence they are good, while P8’s defection remains suspicious.

Cooperate with unobserved P6: mutual cooperation improves good-player welfare, and the prior selfish probability is below the threshold where defection is preferable. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P3’s action. Update identity beliefs from my encounters: players who cooperated against my D are good if selfish players optimize their payoff.
Cooperate with the unobserved opponent: this supports the shared payoff if they are good, and current evidence does not make selfishness likely enough to favor defection.
Cooperate with P4 to support mutual gains among good players; defect if evidence makes selfishness sufficiently likely. Observed cooperation rules out selfishness under payoff-maximizing play.
Cooperate with P7 absent strong evidence they are selfish; update beliefs from observed actions and prioritize welfare of all good players.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when their likely-good status makes cooperation best for good-player welfare; update beliefs from observed actions and treat messages as unverified.

Defect: D strictly maximizes my payoff in this one-shot encounter. P1, P2, and P5’s observed cooperation rules out selfish types; the remaining unobserved players retain symmetric conditional beliefs.
Defect because it pays more than cooperation against either action; update identity beliefs from observed behavior, treating messages as unverified.
Cooperate with unobserved players; defections raise selfishness estimates, while cooperation indicates a good player. Update beliefs as encounters provide evidence.

Cooperate with P4, whose pledge supports mutual gains; update from the actual outcome. Prior cooperation by P1, P2, P7, and P9 is strong evidence they are good, while P8’s defection remains suspicious.
Cooperate with unobserved P1 to support good-player welfare; observed cooperation strongly favors good roles, while P4 and P8’s defections raise concern. Update from future encounters.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. The players who cooperated against my D are not selfish; distribute remaining uncertainty across the unobserved players.
Cooperate with the unobserved opponent: mutual cooperation maximizes the shared payoff if they are good, while observed cooperation identifies the others as good under selfish payoff maximization.
Cooperate with the unobserved P3 to support good players’ shared payoff; update beliefs from observed behavior and defect when evidence indicates a selfish opponent.
Cooperate with P8 absent evidence of selfishness; update beliefs from observed actions and prioritize welfare of all good players.
Defect against an untested opponent when the estimated selfish risk outweighs the welfare benefit of cooperation; update beliefs from observed actions and treat claims as unverified.

Defect in this one-shot encounter; it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. The observed cooperation by P1, P2, P5, and P10 rules out selfish types; remaining unobserved types retain symmetric beliefs.
Defect for the higher immediate payoff against either action; use observed choices to update identity beliefs, treating messages as unverified.
Cooperate with unobserved P10 to support good players’ joint payoff; observed cooperation strongly suggests a good role, while defections raise suspicion. Update after each encounter.
Cooperate with unobserved P3 to support mutual gains among good players. P1, P2, P7, and P9 cooperated, while P4 and P8 defected against my cooperation; update beliefs from further evidence.
Cooperate with unobserved P2; mutual cooperation benefits good players, while observed defections raise suspicion and observed cooperation strongly favors good roles.
Defect for the higher payoff against either action. Players who chose C against my D cannot be selfish; D by P3 does not distinguish selfish from good.
Cooperate with P4: their repeated public willingness to cooperate makes them a plausible good player, and mutual cooperation maximizes good players’ joint payoff.
Cooperate with the unobserved P5 to support mutual gains if they are good; update beliefs from their action and cooperate less readily with players who have defected.
Cooperate with P10 absent strong evidence they are selfish; use observed defections as evidence, not certainty, and prioritize welfare of good players.
Cooperate with untested P9 to support good-player welfare; observed cooperation is evidence of good roles, while defections raise suspicion but are not proof.

Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff in this one-shot encounter. Observed cooperation rules out selfish types for P1, P2, P5, and P10; the remaining unobserved types have symmetric conditional beliefs.
Defect for the higher immediate payoff against either action; update identity beliefs from observed behavior, treating messages as unverified.

Cooperate with P6 absent evidence of selfishness; mutual cooperation best supports good players’ joint payoff. Treat observed defections as evidence, not certainty, and retain uncertainty about unobserved players.
Cooperate with unobserved P5 to support mutual gains among good players; use observed defections to update beliefs and target defection only where selfishness is sufficiently likely.
Cooperate with unobserved P3 to support good-player welfare; prior evidence favors cooperation, while observed defections raise suspicion. Update after the encounter.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P4’s action. Players who chose C against my D cannot be selfish; the remaining uncertainty is among P2, P3, and P4.
Cooperate with P2 while selfishness remains unlikely; C supports the shared payoff if they are good, and I’ll update identity beliefs from observed actions.

Cooperate with P1 absent evidence of defection; mutual cooperation among good players benefits the shared objective. Treat observed defections as evidence of selfishness and cooperation as evidence of being good.
Cooperate with P4 absent strong evidence of selfishness; treat observed defections as evidence, not certainty, and prioritize the welfare of all good players.
Cooperate with untested P8 to support good-player welfare; update identity beliefs from observed actions while treating them as evidence, not proof.
Defect in this one-shot encounter; it maximizes my payoff against either action. The six opponents who cooperated are good; the remaining possible selfish types are among P4, P8, and P9.
Defect for the higher immediate payoff; this is the final encounter, so there is no future reciprocity to consider.
Cooperate with unobserved P7; mutual cooperation best supports good players’ joint payoff. Past defections raise suspicion but are not conclusive.
Cooperate with unobserved P10 to support gains if they are good; observed defections raise suspicion, while cooperation is evidence against selfishness. Update from the final encounter.
Cooperate with unobserved P5 to support good-player welfare; observed defections raise suspicion, while cooperation is strong evidence of good roles.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. Keep uncertainty among P2, P3, and P4; the others cooperated against my defection, while defection alone does not identify a selfish player.
Cooperate with P3 while selfishness is unlikely: C supports the shared payoff if they are good, and costs only one point if they are selfish. Treat observed defections as evidence, not proof.
Cooperate with the unobserved P6: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and no evidence suggests defection. Treat prior defections as evidence, not certainty, and update after the encounter.
Cooperate with P5, whose observed cooperation indicates they are good; prioritize the welfare of all good players.
Cooperate with P9, whose prior cooperation is evidence they are good; on the final round, support good-player welfare and use observed actions to assess roles.

Defect in this final one-shot encounter; D strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. The observed cooperation rules out selfish types; P4 and P8 remain the only possible additional selfish players.
Defect in the final round for the higher payoff against either action. Beliefs reflect observed defections versus cooperation.
Cooperate with P1, whose prior cooperation strongly indicates a good role; mutual cooperation best serves good players. Past defections raise suspicion about P3, P4, and P8.

Choose C with P10, who cooperated previously; mutual cooperation best supports gains among good players. Past defections by P3, P4, and P8 raise suspicion, while cooperation from others is evidence against selfishness.
Defect against P4 given their prior defection and repeated cooperation claims; observed cooperation strongly favors good roles, while defections raise suspicion.
Defect in the final encounter; it yields more than cooperation against either action. C against my D rules out selfish play, while D alone does not identify a selfish player.
Cooperate with P2: their earlier C strongly indicates they are good, and mutual cooperation supports the shared payoff. Treat observed defections as evidence, not proof, of selfishness.
Cooperate with P6, whose prior cooperation suggests they are good; in the final round, mutual cooperation maximizes the good players’ joint payoff.

Cooperated throughout to support good-player welfare. Treated observed defections as evidence of selfishness, but not certainty; cooperation from opponents supported good identities. Treated the leader’s messages as unverified.

Cooperated to support good-player welfare, while treating defections against my cooperation as evidence of selfishness, not proof. Discounted unverified public claims and updated beliefs from observed actions.
Defected in every one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff. Treated observed cooperation as ruling out selfishness; P4 and P8 remain possible selfish players.
Defected throughout to maximize my payoff against either opponent action; treated public cooperation claims as unverified and updated identity beliefs based on observed choices.
Cooperated to support mutual gains among good players; treated defections as evidence of selfishness, while retaining uncertainty because good players may also defect.
Cooperated to support mutual gains among good players; treated repeated cooperation as evidence of good roles and defections against my cooperation as evidence of selfishness.

Cooperated to support good-player welfare, while using defection when facing a likely selfish opponent. Updated role beliefs from observed actions, treating repeated defection as stronger evidence than a single encounter.
Defected in every encounter because it maximized my payoff against either action. Treated opponents who cooperated against my defection as good, leaving uncertainty between P3 and P4.
Cooperated to support the shared payoff among good players, treating defections as evidence of selfishness but not proof.

P1.strategy: Cooperated throughout to support good-player welfare. Treated observed defections as evidence of selfishness, but not certainty; cooperation from opponents supported good identities. Treated the leader’s messages as unverified.
